ledger.note: 1589: Asilah passes to Spain. 'In 1589 the Saadians briefly regained control of Asilah, but then lost it to the Spanish' (no year for the Spanish takeover; the enclaves table has Asilah Spanish 'c. 1604-1691' and Portuguese 1577-1589). The sibling Portuguese and Saadi dossiers date it to 1589.

20 November 1610: Larache is ceded. 'Sultan Muhammad al-Shaykh al-Ma'mun invited Juan de Mendoza y Velasco, Marquis of San German, to take possession of the city'; 'The cession of Larache effectively took place on 20 November 1610'; the Marquis 'took possession of the port on 20 November 1610, meeting no hostilities'.

region.text: La Mamora (Mehdya) at the mouth of the Sebou

ledger.note: August 1614: Spain takes La Mamora. 'A Spanish fleet under Admiral Luis Fajardo captured Al-Ma'mura during the reign of Mulay Zidan in August 1614'; the Spanish 'left a strong garrison of 1,500 men, and called the harbour San Miguel de Ultramar'. The page names no holder; the Saadi dossier has the loss.

1681: Moulay Ismail storms Mehdya. 'The new Sultan Mulay Ismail took the city by storm in 1681, and renamed the city al-Mahdiya'; the Larache siege page: he 'had just taken over al-Mahdya in 1681', under Spanish control 'since 1614'.

November 1689: Larache surrenders. Operations began on 14 July 1689 and the Moroccan army surrounded the city in August; 'Finally on 11 November, the Spanish troops surrendered' (other sources: the assault on 1 November 1689); the garrison of 2,000 soldiers and 200 guns lost 400 killed and 1,600 prisoners.

1692: Moulay Ismail takes Asilah. 'In 1692, the town was taken by the Moroccans under the leadership of Moulay Ismail' (the enclaves table has Spanish rule to 1691; the Larache siege page has a prisoner exchange at Ceuta in September 1691).
1692: the last Spanish post on the Moroccan Atlantic coast falls with Asilah.

wars.name: Moulay Ismail's capture of Mehdya
wars.outcome: Mulay Ismail took the city by storm in 1681; the Moroccans took a statue and prisoners as loot and a ransom was paid later.

wars.name: Siege of Larache
wars.outcome: Operations began on 14 July 1689; the Moroccan army surrounded the city in August and the Spanish garrison of 2,000 men surrendered on 11 November (other sources: 1 November); governor Fernando Villorias y Medrano was captured.

wars.name: Moulay Ismail's capture of Asilah
wars.outcome: 'In 1692, the town was taken by the Moroccans under the leadership of Moulay Ismail.'

certainty.note: Three coastal presidios: the pages give years and no extent; each is a 25 km circle, the grid's minimum, and Mehdya is drawn 9 km off at Kenitra.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for these posts. The Saadi dossier carries the Spanish gains (Asilah 1589, Larache 1610, La Mamora 1614) under the counterpart spanish-empire; this dossier is the state that held them, and those events should read spanish-presidios-of-morocco. The Portuguese Morocco dossier's 1589 loss of Asilah has the same counterpart. Dates in conflict: Asilah to Spain 1589 (Asilah page, the Saadi and Portuguese dossiers) or c. 1604 (enclaves table); Asilah lost 1692 (Asilah page) or 1691 (table; the siege page has a prisoner exchange in September 1691); Larache taken 11 November 1689 or 1 November (siege page); Mehdya 'Portuguese 1515' on the Mehdya page (São João da Mamora) and the English-Dutch pirate battle of about 1610. Not entered, for page budget: Melilla (since 1497), the Peñón de Vélez de la Gomera (1508-1522, since 1564), Alhucemas (table 'since 1559', text 1673), Ceuta (since 1640), Cazaza (1505-1533), Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequena (1510-1644) and Dakhla (1502) of the same enclaves table; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Spain row may carry the Mediterranean ones.
